ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
As shown in the figure, a horizontal conveyor belt moves at a constant speed of $3\mathrm{m/s}$. A small block with a mass of $1\mathrm{kg}$ (which can be considered as a point mass) is gently placed without initial velocity at the left end $A$ of the conveyor belt. After some time, the small block reaches the right end $B$ of the conveyor belt. The distance between $A$ and $B$ is $6\mathrm{m}$, the coefficient of kinetic friction between the small block and the conveyor belt is 0.15, and the gravitational acceleration is $g=10\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$.

1. The time it takes for the small block to move from $A$ to $B$
2. Increasing only the speed of the conveyor belt while keeping other physical quantities unchanged can reduce the time it takes for the small block to move from $A$ to $B$ on the conveyor belt. What should the speed of the conveyor belt be to minimize the movement time of the small block?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, there is a horizontal conveyor belt, with the left end marked as A and the right end marked as B; a small block is placed above the conveyor belt near the left end A, and the upper surface of the conveyor belt moves in the direction from A to B. The problem gives the length AB as L=6 m, the initial speed of the conveyor belt as u=3 m/s, the coefficient of kinetic friction as μ=0.15, and g=10 m/s². Reasoning: When the small block is just gently placed on the conveyor belt, its initial velocity relative to the ground is 0, while the conveyor belt moves to the right, so the small block slides relative to the conveyor belt and is subjected to a kinetic friction force to the right. During the sliding stage, the acceleration of the small block is a=μg=0.15×10=1.5 m/s². 1. When the conveyor belt speed is u=3 m/s, the time required for the small block to accelerate to the same speed as the conveyor belt is t1=u/a=3/1.5=2 s. The displacement of the small block in this stage is x1=u²/(2a)=3²/(2×1.5)=3 m, which is less than AB=6 m, so the small block will first reach the speed of the conveyor belt, and then move uniformly with the conveyor belt. The remaining displacement is 6−3=3 m, and the uniform-motion time is t2=3/3=1 s. The total time is T=t1+t2=2+1=3 s. 2. When only the conveyor belt speed is changed to u, if the small block can catch up with the conveyor belt before reaching B, that is, u²/(2a)≤L, then the total time is T(u)=u/a+(L−u²/(2a))/u=L/u+u/(2a). Find the minimum with respect to u: dT/du=−L/u²+1/(2a)=0, obtaining u²=2aL, so u=√(2aL)=√(2×1.5×6)=√18=3√2 m/s. At this time, the small block just reaches the speed of the conveyor belt at B; if the conveyor belt speed is further increased, the small block moves throughout the entire process with the maximum frictional acceleration, and the shortest time to reach B no longer continues to decrease. Therefore, the critical conveyor belt speed that makes the motion time reach a minimum is 3√2 m/s.
